audit.whatIsWrong: Full phases[0..5].side all read "Skill" and phases[6].side reads "Cassiopeia", while content win[] reads Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Cassiopeia/Aurora/Cassiopeia/Aurora and the packet levelChart matches content exactly. Row 6 is a direct contradiction — the full layer says Cassiopeia wins two-items-in, the content layer says Aurora.
audit.why: phases[N].side and win[N] are the same row. Content and packet agree with each other; the full layer is the stale one. Mechanically the packet chart holds: Aurora owns levels 1-3 (Q at 900 outranges Noxious Blast at 850, Cassiopeia has no dash at any point), Cassiopeia owns 4-5 (Miasma ranked, Q back every 3.5s, Twin Fang healing on poisoned targets) and first item (0.75s Twin Fang against a 7s Q), Aurora takes 6 (Between Worlds) and two items.
audit.corrected: All seven full sides aligned to win[N], with every phases[N].why rewritten in the same proposal to argue the side it now sits under, and ratings moved with them.
sources: cassiopeia kit Q/W/E cooldowns and ranges

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[3].why claimed "three-spell spirit stacks proc your passive haste" (Aurora's passive heals, it grants no haste), breakdown.spikes claimed Luden's "makes the rotation half a bar", and content whys[3] described the level-6 Petrifying Gaze spike under the Levels 4-5 row.
audit.why: Riot's passive text is spirits that follow her and heal her. "Half a bar" is a magnitude with no source. Cassiopeia's R arrives at 6, so it cannot be the reason 4-5 belongs to her; her actual 4-5 spike is Miasma ranking and Twin Fang's 0.75s sustain.
audit.corrected: Spike text rebuilt on real timings: full kit at 3, Between Worlds at 6, Miasma maxed to a 16s cooldown as her spike, and Twin Fang's 0.75s cooldown against Aurora's 7s Q at first item.
sources: aurora kit P and Q cooldowns

audit.whatIsWrong: The two decisive interactions were both absent, and one was asserted backwards. (a) Miasma grounds — and BOTH of Aurora's leaps, W and R, are Movement abilities, so inside the clouds her exit and her ultimate switch off. Not stated anywhere. (b) Petrifying Gaze stuns only enemies FACING Cassiopeia and merely slows anyone with their back turned. Not stated anywhere. Instead, three fields (whys[6], spikes[3].text, late) claim Between Worlds lets you "phase through" Petrifying Gaze — Riot's R text gives a leap, a shockwave, a slowing zone and a cross-zone teleport, and no untargetability at all. Also: Twin Fang's bonus damage is against POISONED targets, and whys[2], whys[5], spikes[2] and mid all wrote "grounded" instead.
audit.why: Riot's W text ends "Grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities", and Aurora's W and R are both leaps. Riot's R text distinguishes stun-if-facing from slow-if-back-turned. Riot's Twin Fang text says increased damage to Poisoned targets and heals her for a percentage of damage dealt.
audit.corrected: Grounding-vs-both-leaps and the facing rule now carried through winCon, cooldowns, dos/donts, mid, late and the level chart; the phase-through-Gaze claim removed rather than restated; "grounded targets" corrected to "poisoned targets" everywhere it appeared.
sources: aurora kit W/R text and dash flags

audit.whatIsWrong: Twin Fang heals Cassiopeia for a percentage of the damage dealt and comes back every 0.75 seconds, but Grievous Wounds appeared only once, in report[8], and there as "anti-heal early into his sustain".
audit.why: The brief's missingInteractions flags needs-antiheal for this matchup: her sustain through chip damage decides extended trades.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds now named in breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.carry, breakdown.feeding, late and report[8].

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all, and wants.you[1] told the reader to all-in "when Noxious Trap is on cooldown" — a fabricated ability name attached to a spell that is back every 3.5 seconds anyway.
audit.why: The cooldown that decides this lane is Miasma at 24/22/20/18/16, because it is the one that removes Aurora's exit. Noxious Blast at 3.5s is never meaningfully down, and Noxious Trap is not a Cassiopeia ability.
audit.corrected: cooldowns rebuilt on Miasma 24s/16s, Twin Fang 0.75s and Petrifying Gaze 80-120s; the all-in trigger moved to Miasma.

audit.why: 52.84% over 405 games is the figure carried in the packet and nothing on the page states a different number.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twelve full-layer fields called Cassiopeia "he/his" — tldr, ahead, loading, breakdown.wave, dosFull[2].t, dontsFull[0].t, dontsFull[2].t, report[8].t, report[11].t and the trade strings.
audit.why: champ-gender lists cassiopeia as female; the owner is addressed as "you", so every third-person pronoun here is Cassiopeia.
audit.corrected: All corrected to she/her in the rewrites below.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[10].t claimed "Your E knockback-slow is clean gank setup" — Aurora's E has no knockback — and ignored that Miasma grounds the jungler too.
audit.why: Riot's E text: damages and slows, then Aurora hops backward. Grounding applies to any Movement ability, so a dash-reliant jungler is caught by the same clouds.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around E's slow and the grounding applying to the gank.

edits.before: Cassiopeia is completely immobile before 6 outside of Twin Fang's minor range extension, so your E dash lets you get in, land Q, and back out clean before she can poison-stack you. Watch her Noxious Trap animation — it's slow and telegraphed, so if you see her cast it early you get a free window to all-in. Keep resetting the poison stacks by disengaging rather than trading through them, since Twin Fang's bonus damage against poisoned targets punishes standing still.
edits.after: Cassiopeia has no dash, so your W leap in and E's backhop out beat anything she can do about the entry — as long as Miasma is not on the ground. That is the whole early lane: her W is 24 seconds at rank 1, and inside those clouds your W and R stop working entirely. Watch for the Noxious Blast delay and step out of the circle rather than tanking it, because Twin Fang's bonus damage only lands on poisoned targets and heals her for a share of what it deals.

edits.before: At level 6 Cassiopeia's Petrifying Gaze becomes a genuine threat: if she gets you facing her at low HP it's a full stun into her burst combo, so respect vision and don't dash blind into unknown positioning around this level. She still has zero gap-close, so if you bait the stun on cooldown or avoid facing her directly you keep winning the neutral. The moment she stacks enough poison and hits her first item spike, her sustained damage against grounded targets starts to edge past your own trading pattern if you let the fight go long.
edits.after: At level 6 Petrifying Gaze is the threat, but read the mechanic exactly: it stuns enemies facing her and only slows those with their backs turned, so the counterplay is to turn and keep walking rather than to trade through it. It is 120 seconds at rank 1, and she has no gap-close, so a Gaze spent on nothing hands you the next two minutes of neutral. What actually beats you is the long fight — Twin Fang's bonus damage on poisoned targets heals her back, so break off and let the poison expire instead of standing in it.

edits.before: Your Between Worlds becomes the deciding factor in the late game — phasing through her Petrifying Gaze cast window completely voids her main teamfight and pick tool, letting you reappear and burst her instead. Outside of that dodge, respect her ability to poison-stack a target across a full fight and just melt them with Twin Fang scaling, so don't stand in extended fights without a plan to phase or disengage.
edits.after: Between Worlds does not phase you out of Petrifying Gaze — it is a leap, and Miasma grounds leaps. What decides the late game is where the fight happens: outside her clouds your W and R both work and she cannot follow either one. Turn away from the Gaze so it slows rather than stuns, and carry Grievous Wounds, because Twin Fang heals her for a share of every tick she lands on a poisoned target.

notes: PACKET SUSPECTNAMES: two of three are real. "Noxious Trap" (spikes[0].text, and repeated in early and wants.you[1]) is not a Cassiopeia ability at all — her Q is Noxious Blast — fixed. "Twin Fang's" in early is a FALSE POSITIVE, that is the correct E name. "Your Between Worlds" in spikes[3] is also a false positive on the name, but the sentence around it was wrong for a different reason and is rewritten. DIFF LEFT ALONE: diff reads TRICKY at 7/10 difficulty and 7.5/10 carry threat against a 52.84% Aurora win rate over 405 games and a level chart that gives Aurora five of seven rows. That reads harsh, but moving diff means moving diffRating, carryRating, breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t together and I have no basis in the kits for a specific new number, so I left the whole group untouched. See questionsForUser. RATING SEMANTICS: I read phases[N].rating as the strength of the named side's edge, not as Aurora-favourability, because elsewhere in this champion's data a row sided to the enemy carries a HIGH rating (aurora vs diana, phases[4] = Diana at 7/10). On that reading the flipped rows move to 6/10 rather than down, and phases[5] needed no change. UNVERIFIED AND NOT WRITTEN: whether Aurora's R can be cast while grounded to teleport across an already-placed zone (the zone teleport may not be a Movement ability even though the initial leap is); whether tenacity, Cleanse or QSS shorten Petrifying Gaze; and whether Aurora's W stealth breaks Cassiopeia's Twin Fang targeting. None of that is in Riot's text and needsResearch is empty by design, so I stated only the facing rule and the grounding, both of which are explicit in the ability text.
